beatOutlines.textOutline: Spotting a bullish crossover on both Stochastics and MACD on the daily chart, Raju eagerly buys.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji immediately warns him to pull up the weekly chart and inspect the macro trend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju bought at ₹148, but the stock collided head-on into weekly resistance and slipped.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Within two sessions price slumped to ₹158 as institutions sold into the counter-trend bounce.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy's rule: the weekly chart dictates trend direction, while the daily chart only tunes entry timing.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Today we dive deep into the second installment of John Murphy's oscillator masterclass.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: We will examine how Lane's Stochastics gauges closing price location and how MACD Histogram leads crossovers.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And finally, multi-timeframe alignment and hunting high-odds reversals with the Principle of Contrary Opinion.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: George Lane's core thesis: in an uptrend prices close near the period high; in a downtrend near the low.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The definitive trade signal occurs when the %K line crosses the %D line beyond the 80 or 20 boundaries.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Larry Williams %R is mathematically identical to Stochastics, but plotted inverted on a 0 to -100 scale.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When %R visits the oversold zone and punches back above -80, it fires an immediate buy trigger.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy states plainly: oscillators are kings in trading ranges, but become subservient in strong trends.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In a powerful runaway trend, an oscillator stays pinned overbought, wiping out counter-trend traders.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Three ideal uses for oscillators: range extremes, trend-aligned pullbacks, and sharp divergence signals.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Gerald Appel's MACD plots the difference between two EMAs, smoothed by a 9-day signal line.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Thomas Aspray introduced the MACD Histogram, plotting the spread between the MACD and Signal lines as bars.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When the histogram slope reverses, it flags the impending crossover days in advance of the actual line cross.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy's multi-timeframe doctrine: the larger timeframe sets the trend; the smaller timeframe executes entries.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When the weekly trend is bullish, ignore daily overbought sells and strictly buy oversold daily dips.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When everyone turns unanimously bullish, the question arises: who is left to buy?
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Bullish sentiment above 80% means all capital is already committed, leaving the market ripe for a top.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy's ironclad rule: never trade on sentiment alone; wait for price to confirm with a chart trendline break.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now your turn. Correctly analyze this multi-timeframe and sentiment setup.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think... resolve the conflict between weekly trend, daily oversold dip, and 85% bullish sentiment.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Do NOT take the daily long! 85% bullish sentiment warns of extreme crowd greed and exhaustion; wait for price breakdown to initiate contrarian shorting.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju opens his trade log and completely restructures his trading process after today's lesson.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji reinforces the definitive execution rule for technical oscillators.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Let us unite all the master principles of Chapter 10 Part 2 into a single cohesive framework.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Slow Stochastics and Williams %R pinpoint overbought and oversold conditions with surgical accuracy in ranges.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The MACD Histogram slope detects deceleration days before the actual signal crossover takes place.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And when over 80% of market participants turn uniformly bullish, recognize that the herd is primed for exhaustion.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Finally discipline and risk management protect your capital in the market.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Remember: The magic of oscillators activates only when you align with weekly trend and refuse to blindly follow the herd.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Slow Stochastics uses %K and %D to locate closes inside recent range
Right-hand %K crossovers beyond 80/20 filter out premature false signals
Larry Williams %R inverts the scale (0 to -100) to gauge close vs period high
Oscillators excel in trading ranges; they must submit to trend in runaway markets
MACD combines trend-following EMAs with an oscillator signal line
MACD Histogram measures the line spread, leading actual signal line crosses
Dual-Timeframe: Weekly chart dictates directional bias, daily times entry pullbacks
Principle of Contrary Opinion: Over 80% consensus marks impending market tops
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
